content.value_statement: Teams need consistent Angular forms with validation, layout, and async options. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through @delon/form patterns.
actual_capabilities: Creates @delon/form SF schemas for strings, numbers, dates, selects, uploads, and boolean controls.
Shows UI schema options for labels, grid spans, placeholders, and responsive layouts.
Defines validation patterns with required fields, min and max rules, formats, and custom validators.
Guides async option loading for autocomplete, dynamic dropdowns, and cascading selects.
Structures multi-step forms with step state and submit flow examples.
limitations: Does not install Angular, ng-alain, or @delon/form dependencies for you.
Examples require adaptation to your services, routes, and design system.
Does not provide backend upload, persistence, or API implementations.
Generated schemas still need accessibility and validation testing in the target app.

use_cases.title: Create Admin CRUD Forms
use_cases.description: Build schema-driven create and edit forms with consistent widgets, validation, and submit handling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Enterprise Forms
use_cases.description: Define shared layout, validation, and widget patterns across many ng-alain screens.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multi-Step Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan wizard-style forms that collect data across steps and review it before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic SF Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an @delon/form SF form for a user profile. Include name, email, role, validation, and a simple responsive layout.

prompt_templates.title: Add Widget-Specific UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an @delon/form schema for a task editor. Use date, select, checkbox, textarea, and number widgets with clear validation.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Async Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an @delon/form pattern for async assignee and city options. Include loading states, debounce guidance, and cascading selection behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a three-step @delon/form wizard for onboarding. Include schemas, state flow, validation boundaries, and final review behavior.

output_examples.input: Request a profile form with basic fields and validation.
output: A clear schema plan for name, email, age, and role fields.
Recommended widgets, required fields, and validation rules.
A responsive layout strategy for labels and controls.

output_examples.input: Ask for dynamic selects backed by service data.
output: A pattern for async option loading and search debounce.
Guidance for mapping service results to labels and values.
Notes for loading states and stale selection handling.

output_examples.input: Request a wizard for collecting onboarding information.
output: A step-by-step workflow outline with separate schema sections.
State management guidance for merging step data.
A final review and submit flow description.

best_practices: Start with JSON Schema requirements before choosing widgets or layouts.
Keep UI schema concerns separate from validation and data shape concerns.
Test async option loading, custom validators, and responsive grids in the target app.
anti_patterns: Do not hide validation rules inside widgets when schema rules can express them.
Do not rely on sample upload actions without a real backend and permission model.
Do not log submitted form data in production applications.

faq.question: What framework does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Angular applications that use ng-alain and the @delon/form SF component.

faq.question: Can it create custom validators?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains custom validator patterns and when to use schema validation instead.

faq.question: Does it include backend API code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on front-end schema forms and integration points for your services.

faq.question: Can it handle async dropdown data?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers async data loading, autocomplete, and cascading select patterns.

faq.question: Is it useful for multi-step forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes wizard patterns with step state, data merging, and review behavior.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
